newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Beijing CITIC sets a winner.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Beijing CITIC sets a winner.

text.p: China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) launched a winner on Wednesday with a US$200 million floating rate note issue.

The five-year notes were priced and re-offered at par to float at 35 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offfered Rate. Fees are 20 basis points to give an all-in return of 39 basis points.
The response to the notes was very positive, with 26 banks joining bookrunner CS First Boston in the syndicate group. Other bankers said they hoped to pick up some paper in the secondary market.
China issues have performed extremely well this year as investors seek out investment-grade opportunities in the region.
With South Korea and Thailand losing their appeal in the wake of banking sector malaise, China's top financial institutions are finding that their issues are in hot demand.
CITIC Beijing is rated Baa1 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard and Poor's Corp.
The company reports directly to the State Council, China's highest governing body. It is the parent of Hong Kong blue chip CITIC Pacific as well as numerous other firms.
At 39 basis points all-in, bankers said the pricing on the CITIC issue was reasonable, especially given the performance of China issues in the secondary market.

China Construction Bank's five-year FRN issued earlier this year paid an all-in of 37.5 basis points. More recently, Bank of China, China's top commercial bank, offered an all-in of 42.5 basis points for seven years.
"The CITIC deal already is bid at 35 basis points in the secondary market," remarked one trader.
In other news, bankers said First Pacific Bank Ltd, a unit of FPB Bank Holding Co Ltd, will launch a multi-tranche floating rate certificates of deposit (FRCD) issue shortly.
The certificates will be available in either Hong Kong or U.S. dollars.
Bankers said the issue size is expected to be HK$500 million or its equivalent in U.S. dollars. It will carry a maturity of five years with put and call options in years three and four.
Standard Chartered Bank, Westdeutsche Landesbank, Bayerische Landesbank and CS First Boston are the mandated arrangers.
Sources said Chungtex Electronic Co Ltd has mandated Citicorp International to arrange a US$25 million floating rate note issue.
They said the facility has a final maturity of three years with annual put options.
